newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK admits some Vietnamese will remain after 1997.
newsitem.headline: HK admits some Vietnamese will remain after 1997.

text.p: Hong Kong admitted on Saturday it was unlikely to be able to clear its detention centres of Vietnamese boatpeople before the handover to China later this year.

The British colony's Secretary for Security, Peter Lai, told a news conference that Hong Kong had been forced to make provisions to continue to pay for the upkeep of asylum seekers beyond the handover because Vietnam is dragging its heels on accepting many of them back.

China has told the departing British the camps must be cleared before Hong Kong reverts to its rule at midnight on June 30, but has not said publicly what it would do if the colonial government fails to comply.

"We are not budgeting in such a way that we will completely exhaust every single dollar within our budget on the 1st of July 1997. we cannot be as brave as that. We have to be a bit more prudent," Lai said.
He said Hong Kong had budgeted about HK$137 million ($17.7 million) for caring for the boatpeople, he said.

Hong Kong plans to ask Sadako Ogata, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) who starts a three-day visit here on Sunday, to step up efforts to resettle the boatpeople and has urged Vietnam to take them back.
About 5,500 Vietnamese boatpeople remain in Hong Kong, the last of a human floodtide of tens of thousands who fled their homeland after the communist victory in 1975.
Vietnam is refusing to take about about half of those remaining, most of whom are ethnically Chinese rather than Vietnamese.
